15: She blesses after lighting, because if she blesses it becomes an acceptance of Shabbat and it would be forbidden to light. Therefore on Yom Tov, she should bless and then light - this was written in the [introduction to the] Drisha in the name of his mother. But woman have no intelligence, etc. Our sages made no distinction between these cases, as we see in siman 158, see there, and the Tosafot in Pesachim 7b.

And to make a blessing on it. Because lighting [Shabbat] candles is obligatory, for the sake of peace at home (shalom bayit), that one not trip over wood or stone (Mordechai). And even those who say that the candle of Yom Kippur does not require a blessing, in any case, here it is used for the necessities of eating—preparing their utensils and dishes, which is not the case on Yom Kippur. And all the more so for us, who believe that one does make a blessing on Yom Kippur, because we think that shalom bayit applies even without eating (Mahari”l, Responsa, No. [144] 155).
